extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners / practitioners attending USPTO subject-matter-eligibility training
extracted.subtask_description: Workshop materials for analyzing patent claims under USPTO subject-matter-eligibility guidance (July 2015 Update / 2014 Interim Guidance), using an attached Subject Matter Eligibility Worksheet to evaluate original and amended claims for abstract-idea issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply July 2015 Update: Subject Matter Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: This workshop training will demonstrate the application of several key aspects of the July 2015 Update: Subject Matter Eligibility (July 2015 Update).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Walk through analysis of a select group of claims from the published examples found in the July 2015 Update Appendix 1: Examples using the Subject Matter Eligibility Worksheet. The workshop training aims to demonstrate how the July 2015 Update principles are applied in practice to sample claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze examples under the 2014 Interim Guidance on Patent Subject Matter Eligibility (IEG)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examples should be analyzed under the 2014 Interim Guidance on Patent Subject Matter Eligibility (IEG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When performing the eligibility analysis for the example claims, apply the steps, concepts, and tests set forth in the 2014 IEG. Use the IEG framework as the primary analytical standard for determining abstract-idea/judicial-exception issues in these examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Subject Matter Eligibility Worksheet (Abstract Idea Workshop) for claim analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Please analyze claim 1 using the attached Subject Matter Eligibility Worksheet (Subject Matter Eligibility Worksheet - Abstract Idea Workshop).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both the original and amended claims provided in the examples are to be analyzed by completing the worksheet. The worksheet captures the stepwise analysis (identification of the abstract idea/judicial exception and evaluation of additional elements) that the workshop demonstrates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Quick Reference Sheet graphic to identify abstract ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: The graphic on page 2 of the July 2015 Update: Interim Eligibility Guidance Quick Reference Sheet may also be used as a guide for identifying abstract ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Quick Reference Sheet's graphic to help classify claim subject matter into categories of abstract ideas and to guide identification of judicial exceptions when completing the worksheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat Appendix examples as illustrative and fact-specific
rubrics_metrics.description: The examples are intended to be illustrative only; they should be interpreted based on the fact patterns set forth below. Other fact patterns may have different eligibility outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not generalize the outcome of an example beyond the specific disclosed facts. If material facts change, the eligibility conclusion may change; therefore analyze the precise fact pattern given in each example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus solely on subject-matter-eligibility for the workshop (exclude other patentability requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of this workshop, other patentability requirements under §§ 102, 103, 112 and 101 (utility, inventorship, double patenting) and non-statutory double patenting need not be addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the workshop analysis, do not evaluate novelty, nonobviousness, written description/enablement, utility, inventorship, or double-patenting issues — concentrate only on subject-matter-eligibility questions per the IEG and July 2015 Update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze original and amended claims independently using the worksheet
rubrics_metrics.description: Please analyze claim 1 (original) and amended claim 1 using the attached Subject Matter Eligibility Worksheet (Separate Worksheet prompts are provided for original and amended claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat claim versions (original, amended/newly added) as separate analysis targets: apply the worksheet and Quick Reference guidance to each claim version to determine whether amendments affect the subject-matter-eligibility outcome.
